speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; tell me, how long has this lesion been present, and did it start as a blister, insect bite, or a small cut?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

Based on the history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the lesion starting at a site of minor trauma (ant bite) and rapidly expanding into a painful ulcer, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum. I have already asked one question regarding the onset; do you have any recent fevers, weight loss, or other signs of infection, and would you like me to request a skin biopsy or blood work to rule out other causes?
